paper.title: Preseason maize and wheat yield forecasts for early warning of crop failure

findings: Public implementation is not a portable end-to-end pipeline: private absolute paths; processed FAO anomaly files, geographic masks, yield preprocessing and expected forecast directories absent.
Historical ENSO conditioning reads ERSSTv5_NINO34.csv. NOAA identifies ERSSTv5 as an in-situ-only SST product; this is not direct validation of incremental satellite OISST.

ENSO future probabilities come from NOAA/CIRES model-analog forecasts. Modern analog initialization uses SST and sea-surface-height fields, and historical hindcasts use CERA-20C; the crop code does not isolate a satellite contribution.
fao_parallel.py removes the target year but retains later years from training. This is leave-one-year-out evaluation, not chronological forward forecasting.

Processed yield anomalies use Gaussian smoothing (sigma three years). Preprocessing is not supplied; supplied code cannot establish that trends or anomaly thresholds were estimated using only earlier labels. The methods describe whole-series smoothing, which is unsuitable for directly asserting real-time causal labels.
Fcst_evaluation.py defaults analogOps to Obs, the explicitly perfect-ENSO sensitivity. Blind execution would not reproduce an operational forecast.
The paper evaluates probabilistic classification with AUC and reliability. It does not establish superiority to a strong ground-weather forecast or realized monetary decision value.

A clean chronological OISST-to-crop-failure experiment is feasible using existing local FAO and OISST snapshots, but would be a new predeclared experiment with training-only detrending/thresholds and proper probability scores, not a direct reproduction or certified satellite result.
interpretation: Useful scientific motivation for a predeclared probabilistic crop-risk experiment. It does not satisfy the user requirement for locally verified satellite forecast usefulness.
